Predictive Distributions of a New Response

Source: R/predict_objects.R
predictive_distributions.Rd

The argument predictive of prediction_interval() takes an object that selects how the estimation uncertainty enters the distribution of a new response. There are three.

pred_averaged()

the default: the family averaged over the approximate sampling distribution of the estimates. It costs one evaluation of the covariance of the estimates.

pred_plugin()

the family at the estimates, ignoring their error. It costs one evaluation of the predictors.

pred_bootstrap()

the parametric bootstrap predictive distribution, by simulation and refit of n responses. It costs n refits, each as expensive as a fit with the hyperparameters held (refit = "coefficients") or as a whole fit (refit = "full").

Value

Not applicable: this topic describes the constructors. Each returns an S7 object that inherits from predictive_type().

Details

A new observation varies for three reasons: the family itself, the effects of a new group where random sets them aside, and the error in the estimates. The first two are random in the model and always enter. The third enters according to the predictive object, for every parameter alike, whether the family has one parameter (a Poisson) or several, and whether or not a parameter has covariates.

Averaged

The family is averaged over the predictors at the fit's estimates with the covariance of the estimates from vcov.StatmodFit() plus the covariance that the effects add. This is the normal approximation to the parametric bootstrap predictive distribution of Harris (1989): the estimates are averaged over their approximate sampling distribution, centered at the fit. For a Gaussian with a constant \(\sigma = e^{\gamma_0}\), \(\hat\gamma_0\) of variance \(v\), the variance of a new observation is \(\mathrm{se}_0^2 + z^\top\Sigma_b z + \hat\sigma^2 e^{2v}\), where the last term is the average of \(\hat\sigma^{*2}\) over that distribution. The argument type of predict.StatmodFit(), the variance type of vcov.StatmodFit(), is read only with this predictive.

Plug-in

The family at the estimates, averaged only over the effects: the estimative interval, which ignores the error in the estimates and so covers less than the level in a small sample.

Bootstrap

The parametric bootstrap predictive distribution itself: n responses are simulated from the fit with the random effects drawn afresh, each response is refitted, and the family at each refit is averaged over the effects. refit = "coefficients" refits at the fit's hyperparameters; "full" chooses them again on every replica, so their uncertainty enters too, at the cost of a whole fit each. The bootstrap is rejected for a model with a block that moves with its coefficients (modelterms7::seg(), modelterms7::jump(), modelterms7::jseg(), modelterms7::nl()), for a response that is not one number per observation, and, with refit = "full", for a cross-validated criterion. A replica whose refit fails is left out, with a warning that reports how many were. The seed is the caller's: set.seed() before the call fixes the replicas. See predictive_bootstrap().

Hyperparameters

The interval for a new group (group_interval()) is conditional on the covariance that the fit estimated, and so is the interval for a new observation, so the uncertainty of the hyperparameters is not propagated. The exception is pred_bootstrap() with refit = "full", where the hyperparameters are chosen again on every replica.

References

Harris, I. R. (1989). Predictive fit for natural exponential families. Biometrika, 76, 675–684.

See also

pred_averaged(), pred_plugin(), pred_bootstrap(), prediction_interval(), predict_intervals.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(40))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(40, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
nd <- data.frame(x = 0.5)
for (p in list(pred_averaged(), pred_plugin())) {
  print(predict(fit, what = "response", newdata = nd,
                interval = prediction_interval(predictive = p)))
}
#>        fit        se     lower   upper
#> 1 1.529108 0.3423082 0.8547573 2.20346
#>        fit        se     lower    upper
#> 1 1.529108 0.3337831 0.8749056 2.183311
